title: Perforated Metal vs Expanded Metal: Key Differences
excerpt: Both give you an open, lightweight metal sheet — but they are made differently and behave differently. Here is how to choose between them.
cover_alt: Close-up of round-hole perforated metal sheet
meta_title: Perforated Metal vs Expanded Metal: Key Differences | JASSCO
meta_description: How perforated and expanded metal are made, how they differ in open area, material use, strength and appearance, and how to choose for your application.
content:
Perforated metal and expanded metal are both used where a metal sheet needs openings — for airflow, light, drainage, visibility or weight saving. They look similar from a distance, but they are produced in very different ways, and that affects cost, strength and appearance.

How perforated metal is made

Perforated metal starts as a solid sheet or coil. A press punches holes through it in a repeating pattern. The punched-out material (the slug) is removed, so the finished sheet is flat and keeps its original thickness and dimensions.

Because the holes are tooled, you can specify the hole shape — round, square, slotted, hexagonal or decorative — the hole size, the pitch (the distance between hole centres) and the arrangement, such as a straight, staggered or triangular pitch. Plain, unperforated margins can be left around the edges or in specific areas.

How expanded metal is made

Expanded metal is made by slitting the sheet and stretching it in one operation. Nothing is punched out: the strands and bonds stay joined and form diamond-shaped openings. Expanded mesh can be supplied in its standard (raised) form, flattened by rolling, or in heavier grating forms.

The main differences

Perforated metalExpanded metal
ProcessHoles punched out of solid sheetSheet slit and stretched
Opening shapeRound, square, slotted, hexagonal, decorativeDiamond
Material usePunched material becomes scrapNo material removed
SurfaceFlatRaised strands, unless flattened
Design controlPrecise hole size, pitch and plain marginsDefined by strand width and mesh pitch

Which should you choose?

  • Choose perforated metal when you need a precise, repeatable pattern, a flat surface, plain margins or a specific open area — for example acoustic panel facings, equipment guards, filters and architectural panels.
  • Choose expanded metal when you want a rigid, lightweight mesh with good open area — for example guards, fencing panels, ceilings, facade screens and filter supports.

Load-bearing uses such as walkways or platforms must always be designed and verified by a qualified engineer for the specific application.

What to send for a quotation

For perforated sheet: material grade, thickness, sheet or coil size, hole shape and size, pitch and arrangement, required open area and plain margins. For expanded mesh: material grade, thickness, strand width, mesh pitch, form (raised, flattened or grating), sheet size and orientation.
